html:
SMTO-FIL-0016 — SMTO expected a folder but found a file

GUID: 915ebbe4-51b1-4dc4-bef2-87689ac22f51
Slug: file-not-a-directory
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • SMTO tried to use a location as a folder, for example to list it or create something inside it, but that location, or part of it, is a file.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look at the location in Technical details. If it is a file, tell SMTO the folder that contains it instead. SMTO can only list or add things inside a folder, not inside a file.
  2. If you wanted a new folder there, choose a different name, because a file with that name already exists in that spot. A folder can't be created where a file already uses the same name.
  3. If you meant to work with the file itself, ask SMTO to read or open that file rather than list it. Reading is the right action for a file; listing only works for folders.

What success looks like

  • SMTO lists the folder's contents or creates the folder, and this message doesn't appear again.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete or rename the existing file to make room unless you're sure it isn't needed, and don't point a saved Run at a different folder without deciding that on purpose.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file operation that requires a directory (file.list, file.mkdir, or traversal through a path component) found a non-directory at that path or received ENOTDIR/ERROR_DIRECTORY from the OS.

What this means

  • A directory-requiring operation found a non-directory resource, or the OS returned its not-a-directory error. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A directory-requiring operation found a non-directory resource, or the OS returned its not-a-directory error.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact component and current resource type on the Gateway.

How to fix it

  • Check path_context/resolved_path in the receipt and stat the path on the Gateway. Use a directory path for file.list or file.mkdir, use file.read/file.stat for a regular file, and correct any parent component that is a file (gateway_core/file_mutate.mkdirs, file_walk.listing, file_common.error_kind).
  • Select a directory or use the operation appropriate for a file.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended directory exists and remains within the accepted path scope.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
